explanation.text: A contrast pairs the same feature in the two neurone types. A cell body can lie between an axon and a dendron without dividing the axon into two; distinguish those structures when describing the sensory neurone.

stem.text: Fig. 10.1 is a graph of an action potential in a mammalian neurone.

stem.text: With reference to Fig. 10.1 suggest why:

items: no further action potential can occur during A and B
it is difficult for a further action potential to occur during C.

points.text: Na+ / sodium, channels already open OR Na+ has already entered neurone OR no more Na+ channels to open OR less Na+ outside to diffuse in OR less steep Na+ concentration gradient ;

B – any one reason from:
sodium channels are, inactive / unresponsive OR potassium channels are open OR membrane is, impermeable / less permeable, to Na+ OR membrane is more permeable to K+ ;

C – any one reason from:
harder to reach threshold OR potassium channels are (still) open OR sodium-potassium pumps need to restore the resting potential ;

explanation.text: An action potential requires sufficient available voltage-gated sodium channels and a threshold depolarisation. Channel inactivation prevents immediate re-excitation; later, a more negative starting potential increases the depolarisation needed to reach threshold.

reasoningChain: Relate each labelled phase to its channel state.
Distinguish channel unavailability from an increased distance to threshold.

bullets: Few candidates were able to fully contrast the structure and function of the two types of neurone. Often one neurone was correctly described without the contrasting description for the other neurone. Common errors were to describe the sensory neurone cell body as being in the middle of the axon rather than being situated between the axon and dendron in the neurone, and to suggest that motor neurones have dendrons. The question command to ‘contrast’ meant that writing similarities such as ‘both have…’ could not gain credit.

Most candidates were able to use the data in the table to describe the relationships between myelination and impulse transmission speed and axon diameter and impulse transmission speed, often supporting their conclusions with correct paired data from the table. Some omitted reference to ‘speed’ which was essential to the answer.

Many candidates made insufficient use of the graph to explain why further action potentials were not possible. Many candidates did not mention the letters A, B and C at all, or combined A and B together in their answer, as though the ion channels opening and closing during A (depolarisation) were the same as those that open and close during B (repolarisation). The commonest correct answer was reference to hyperpolarisation at C.
